title: Release ahead of the schema freeze
lead: Publish a release of main before the v1 schema freeze (sq-12), once the null-spelling bounds (sq-42) and their other-distinct count (sq-43) are in, so consumers can drop constants they now repeat from the 0.2.0 internals and take the shared prefix reader (sq-40). Main is 39 commits past v0.2.0 and binary-breaking (sq-38 to sq-41), so the release notes list the breaking changes. **Not in this slice:** the schema freeze itself.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: A downstream consumer pins 0.2.0 and hard-codes the null-spelling bound (64) and one spelling-count gap that sq-42 and sq-43 were built to remove; nothing it can take has them yet. Found in a consumer review, 2026-10-30.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `Directory.Build.props` (`<Version>` 0.3.0), every golden descriptor (they record the tool version), docs/getting-started.md (the `squalify --version` output), docs/user-guide.md (the "Breaking changes in 1.0.0 (library, unreleased)" and "API added in 1.0.0" entries become 0.3.0), docs/how-it-works.md (banner status; re-render html and pdf), README and design.md only where they name the version or call these changes unreleased 1.0.0 work
- Release notes text (a file in the scratchpad, applied to the GitHub release with `gh release edit` after the release job creates it): a breaking-changes section for a consumer upgrading from 0.2.0

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- A docs test (or the existing release checks) fails while the guides still label the current changes as unreleased 1.0.0 work or show another tool version than `<Version>`.
- `squalify --version` prints 0.3.0 and the golden descriptors record 0.3.0 (the golden update diff changes only the tool version value).
- The workflow check passes: the tag `v0.3.0` equals `<Version>`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Bump `<Version>` to 0.3.0 and re-record the goldens (`SQUALIFY_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 dotnet test squalify.sln -c Release --filter "Category!=Corpus&Category!=Large"`); the diff must change only the `version` inside the one-line `"tool": { ... }` in each golden.
2. Relabel the docs: the guides name 0.3.0 for the changes now on main; keep sq-12 (schema freeze) and 1.0.0 as future work; update `squalify --version` samples; how-it-works banner "v0.3.x"; re-render.
3. Write the breaking-changes release notes for a 0.2.0 consumer (every breaking change on main since v0.2.0: the user guide lists them) and the "API added" list.
4. The orchestrator then commits, waits for CI, tags v0.3.0 (owner pre-authorized the tag once green) and verifies the Release run and both packages on nuget.org; the notes are applied to the GitHub release.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Build, test and format pass (CI filter and with GITHUB_ACTIONS=true); `slicer check` passes; the Package tests pass; CI green on main before the tag; the Release run and both nuget.org packages verified after.
